generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: APPLE'S TERNUS TAKES THE REINS AS CEO, WITH AI AS JOB NO. 1
Summary: John Ternus will step into his new role as Apple's chief executive officer on September 1. Ternus has spent 25 years helping Apple perfect its devices. Apple is set to soon roll out its annual fall products, with this year's lineup including the company's first foldable iPhone, a smart display, AirPods with cameras, a camera-equipped pendant, and more. The releases are crucial to the company's plans to extend its decades-long run of success in the AI era.

Editorial idea:
A leadership change places Apple's next product cycle under an urgent mandate to compete in the AI era.

Central subject:
Apple's incoming CEO John Ternus

Visual relationship:
A long-established device maker handing its controls to a new leader while a demanding AI transition approaches.

Composition:
Show a ceremonial transfer of a precise mechanical control from one set of hands to another, with a series of familiar product silhouettes extending into an unfinished path ahead. Keep the emphasis on succession and forward pressure rather than depicting a generic executive portrait.

Permitted literal elements:
Two sets of hands representing outgoing and incoming leadership
A precisely machined control or baton being transferred
Subtle silhouettes of a foldable phone, smart display, earbuds, and pendant
An unfinished path suggesting the upcoming product cycle

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Artist imitation
Rendered text
Logos
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Making the image a generic corporate succession scene without product-cycle pressure
Treating AI as a decorative visual rather than the stated job priority
Showing unannounced products as finalized or physically specific designs
Using recognizable Apple branding or rendered labels

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
